clue.text: Almost change it in a month's completion

indicators.note: in tells us one group of letters sits inside the month's name

parts.note: May is a month of the year

indicators.note: almost means the word is not quite complete, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: to change is to turn

explanation.surface: Someone almost alters something by the end of a month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' trims TURN to TUR; with IT that goes 'in' MAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Maturity is the state of full development, the point at which growth is complete.

clue.text: Oven joint's right off

indicators.note: off means the letter for right is taken away from the joint

parts.note: a joint of meat cooked in the oven is a roast

explanation.surface: A cook notices the joint in the oven is not quite right.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'joint's' stands for 'is'. 'Off' takes R out of ROAST.
explanation.definitionFit: An oast is a kiln, an oven for drying hops.

clue.text: Illegal delivery capsizing in billabong

indicators.note: capsizing turns a boat upside down, so in a down clue the letters are read backwards
in says the letters are found inside the word billabong

explanation.surface: A boat overturns in an Australian waterhole.
explanation.walkthrough: A billabong is an Australian pool or backwater. Inside it sit LLABON; 'capsizing' turns them round.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a no-ball is a delivery bowled illegally, giving the batting side a run.

clue.text: Tragic character in centre of Jakarta, without wife, missing son

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Tragic character in centre of Jakarta, without wife, missing son', has no parse giving KING LEAR: no clue word supplies the letters before W and S are removed; probably an OCR or setting error, not found by search.
annotationWithheld.clue: Tragic character in centre of Jakarta, without wife, missing son

clue.text: Foreign aid creates and destroys

indicators.note: foreign suggests something strange or unfamiliar, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Overseas aid both builds things up and tears them down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foreign' signals that AIDCREATES is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To eradicate is to wipe out completely, i.e. to destroy.

clue.text: Louts speak up about house with nothing in

indicators.note: about means the reversed word goes around the other letters
up in a down clue means the word is written upwards, backwards

parts.note: to speak is to say

indicators.note: in puts the nothing inside the house abbreviation

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Rowdy people shout about a house that has nothing inside it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' turns SAY to YAS; HO with O 'in' it is HOO, and YAS goes 'about' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Yahoos are coarse, brutish people, from the savage creatures in Gulliver's Travels.

clue.text: May, possessing appeal, eggs on lover

indicators.note: possessing means the first word holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: may, in the sense of being permitted, can stand for can
SA is short for sex appeal
ova are eggs

explanation.surface: A woman called May, being attractive, encourages her boyfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May' looks like a name or the month; it is the verb, CAN. SA, sex appeal, goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Giacomo Casanova was a famous Venetian seducer, so his name means a great womaniser.

clue.text: The most wacky, but not the most extreme, hosts

indicators.note: not the most extreme means the outermost letters at each end are removed

parts.note: barmy means wacky or crazy, so the most wacky is the barmiest

explanation.surface: A remark about the craziest people, though not the most extreme ones.
explanation.walkthrough: BARMY is British slang for crazy. 'Not the most extreme' takes away its superlative's first and last letters, B and T.
explanation.definitionFit: Hosts, as in multitudes, are great armies; the heavenly host is an army of angels.

clue.text: Sally and Dorian getting drunk

indicators.note: someone getting drunk staggers about, so the letters reel into a new order

explanation.surface: Two friends, Sally and Dorian, go out drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sally' looks like a woman's name; it is the definition, a sortie. 'Getting drunk' rearranges DORIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A sally is a sudden attack or foray, and an inroad is a raid into enemy territory.

clue.text: Stop perfectly, but not fully

indicators.note: not fully means the word is incomplete, losing its final letter

parts.note: quite can mean perfectly or completely

explanation.surface: An instruction to halt completely, though not quite all the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not fully' drops the last letter, E.
explanation.definitionFit: To quit is to stop doing something.

clue.text: Andromeda galaxy's beginning to disintegrate in the end

indicators.note: something that disintegrates breaks apart, so these letters fall into a new order
beginning means just the first letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: An astronomer predicts the Andromeda galaxy will start to fall apart eventually.
explanation.walkthrough: ANDROMEDA plus G, the first letter of 'galaxy's', 'to disintegrate' gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Armageddon is the final battle at the end of the world, so the end of everything.

clue.text: Poet runs into watch

indicators.note: into means the first piece goes inside the second

parts.note: a vigil is a watch kept through the night
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A poet runs headlong into a night watchman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Into' puts R inside VIGIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Virgil was the Roman author of the Aeneid.

clue.text: It gives you terribly frail guts, see

definitions.text: It gives you terribly frail guts, see

indicators.note: terribly suggests the letters are badly mangled into a new order

parts.note: see sounds like the letter C, its name when spoken

explanation.surface: A warning that something will leave your stomach in a weak state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terribly' rearranges FRAILGUTS plus C. The whole clue also describes the illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Gastric flu is a stomach bug causing sickness and diarrhoea, leaving the gut weak.

clue.text: Operate drill

definitions.meaning: to operate, to use or put into effect, as in exercising a right
a drill is a practice routine or training task

explanation.definitionFit: To exercise a power is to use it, and an exercise is a training routine like a military drill.

clue.text: I agree; no woman should be contradicted

parts.note: the opposite of no is yes, as the clue's call to contradict asks
the opposite of woman is man, again by contradiction

explanation.surface: A man assents and insists that no woman should ever be argued with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Should be contradicted' tells you to swap 'no' and 'woman' for their opposites. 'I agree' is what a sycophant always says.
explanation.definitionFit: A sycophant who always says I agree to a superior is called a yes-man.

clue.text: Jailhouse rock?

parts.note: the Elvis song title read literally: a rocky island that served as a prison

explanation.definitionFit: Alcatraz is a rocky island in San Francisco Bay that housed a notorious federal prison.

clue.text: Cave is reached, occupied by Resistance

indicators.note: occupied by means the second piece is inside the first

parts.note: to have reached a place is to have got to it
R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A hideout is found, taken over by Resistance fighters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Occupied by' puts R inside GOT TO.
explanation.definitionFit: A grotto is a small cave, often a picturesque one.

clue.text: Regiment trained common characters in grandiose reasoning

indicators.note: trained suggests the letters are drilled into a new formation
the letters common to both words are kept, and the D of grandiose has no partner in reasoning

explanation.surface: A regiment is trained in pompous, overblown thinking.
explanation.walkthrough: Letters shared by GRANDIOSE and REASONING are GRANIOSE (D is in only the first); 'trained' rearranges them.
explanation.definitionFit: To regiment is to organise strictly, imposing order on people or things.

clue.text: Wound not dressed after surgery, originally

indicators.note: after puts the undressed word behind that first letter
originally means only the first letter of the word is used

parts.note: someone not dressed is naked

explanation.surface: A wound is left undressed after an operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wound' reads as an injury, but it is the past tense of wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Wound, past tense of wind, means twisted along, as a path or a serpent did.

clue.text: I could hold drink (Tom can't, by contrast)

parts.note: Tom the cartoon cat is partnered and contrasted with Jerry the mouse
by contrast, the opposite of can't is the plain word can

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of holding their drink, unlike their friend Tom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By contrast' swaps Tom for his cartoon rival, and can't for its opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: A jerrycan is a flat-sided container for carrying fuel or water.

clue.text: Lure serpent rapidly towards the centre

indicators.note: the letters are found in the middle of the phrase, spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A snake moves swiftly to the middle to tempt its prey.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit inside 'serpent rapidly'.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrap is to lure someone into a trap or compromising position.

clue.text: Poles binged endlessly after hiding officer

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Poles binged endlessly after hiding officer', gives no ENSIGN: BINGED trimmed is INGE, which cannot surround NS to give the answer without an anagram signal; probably an OCR misread, not found by search.
annotationWithheld.clue: Poles binged endlessly after hiding officer

clue.text: Substitute trapezes, essentially defective, broken

indicators.note: broken means the remaining letters are smashed into a new order
the word lacks its essence, the two letters at its very centre

explanation.surface: Replacement trapezes are faulty at the core and break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Essentially defective' removes the central PE of TRAPEZES, leaving TRAZES; 'broken' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ersatz describes an inferior imitation used as a substitute for the real thing.

clue.text: Checks on what's in store

parts.note: read as checks on future events, but literally inspections of goods held in a shop's store

explanation.definitionFit: Stocktakes are counts of goods held in stock by a shop or business.

clue.text: Lush women in love

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Lavish women in love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lush' looks like an adjective meaning luxuriant; it is a noun, a drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A lush is a heavy drinker, and a wino is an alcoholic who drinks cheap wine.

clue.text: One held by police raised a cry

indicators.note: held by means the first piece is inside the second
raised in a down clue means the letters are written upwards, backwards

parts.note: the law is slang for the police
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone arrested by the police shouted out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised' turns LAW into WAL, which holds I.
explanation.definitionFit: A wail is a long, high-pitched cry of grief or pain.

clue.text: Plant deaths laid at odd positions

indicators.note: only the letters at the first, third, fifth and further odd places of the run are taken

explanation.surface: A gardener lays flowers at the scene of deaths.
explanation.walkthrough: The odd letters of 'deaths laid at' spell the answer, with 'at' itself joining the run: its A is the eleventh letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The dahlia is a garden plant with large showy flowers.

clue.text: Most unusual, like the H in Morse

definitions.meaning: most eccentric or crazy, the superlative of dotty
the letter H in Morse code is four dots, so it is made entirely of dots

explanation.definitionFit: Dotty means eccentric, and H in Morse code is the code sign most full of dots, four in a row.
